task_description: VectorPilot AI — Dev Tool Launch. lead
requirements:
You’re launching VectorPilot, a CLI and dashboard that auto‑generates API clients from OpenAPI specs and keeps them in sync across repos. The page must explain the core value in under 8 seconds: “Ship integrations faster. No drift.” Include a hero with a concise promise, three outcome‑focused benefits, and a 60‑second product tour video. Add a comparison table against manual client maintenance and codegen scripts. Include an opt‑in lead form for “engineering managers” and “platform teams” with a single job‑role dropdown and work email only; no account creation or stored data, just a Zapier handoff to your CRM. Add social proof: three one‑sentence quotes (with permission) and recognizable logos from design partners. Include a brief “How it works” with a 1‑2‑3 diagram, a security notes section (permissions, read‑only tokens), and a pricing teaser with “contact sales” as the next step. Finish with an FAQ covering language support, monorepo setups, and licensing, then a short trust statement about uptime and support SLAs to reinforce buyer confidence.

Brand vibe: Minimal and technical, expressed with clean typography, disciplined spacing, and terse copy.

Constraints: Include comparison table, FAQ, and a short video embed.
title: VectorPilot AI — Dev Tool Launch

requirements:
LumenPay targets startups paying global contractors in stablecoins while accounting in fiat. The landing must explain compliance, speed, and predictable fees for founders and finance leads. Open with a trust‑forward headline, then three outcome cards: “fewer payment failures,” “faster cross‑border payouts,” “clean books.” Add a region coverage map with tooltips for supported rails and KYC tiers. Include a fee calculator that takes monthly contractor count and average payout but does not store inputs—compute client‑side and reset on refresh. Collect leads through a short form gated by work email and employee count; forward submissions to HubSpot only. Add a SOC 2/ISO note with link to a public security overview PDF. Provide two mini case snippets with quantified outcomes, a brief “How it reconciles in QuickBooks/Xero,” and an “Implementation in 48 hours” section detailing onboarding steps. Close with an FAQ about jurisdictional limits and tax documentation, plus a compliance footnote referencing disclosures so legal review is straightforward.

Brand vibe: Trustworthy and precise, with restrained visuals and copy that favors numbers over hype.

Constraints: Include non-persistent fee calculator and integration badges.
title: LumenPay — Contractor Crypto Payroll

requirements:
CrispClinic offers asynchronous primary care with 2‑hour clinician responses for common conditions. This page recruits early users in approved states. Lead with a single promise and an eligibility checker that runs client‑side: select state, condition, and pharmacy preference; show “eligible/ineligible” without storing data. Explain care flow with three steps, display price transparency (flat visit fee), and list included services and exclusions. Provide “Clinician credentials” and “Data use” sections in plain language. Add testimonials placeholders and a HIPAA statement linking to a public Notice of Privacy Practices PDF. Include a waitlist form with name, email, and state; submissions go to your mailing list only, no account created. Add a small “Why now” note on access gaps and response time. End with an FAQ on refunds, prescriptions, and telehealth limitations, plus a safety disclaimer on emergencies and urgent symptoms to set expectations clearly.

Brand vibe: Calm and clinical, emphasizing clarity, reassurance, and ethical handling of information.

Constraints: Show eligibility UI but do not persist inputs; include state availability map and transparent pricing.
title: CrispClinic — Telehealth Beta Waitlist

requirements:
AeroNest partners with airlines and boutique hotels to offer a co‑branded card focused on off‑peak award availability. The page must position the benefit clearly: “More seats when others say sold out.” Include a hero with APR disclosure link, three benefit tiles (off‑peak unlocks, lounge day‑passes, elite‑match trials), and a redemption explainer with a simple route example. Add partner logos and a rotating carousel of sample award prices. Provide an “Am I a fit?” checklist for frequent leisure travelers. Collect nonbinding early applications with name, email, self‑reported credit score range, and travel frequency; send to your CRM via webhook and show a confirmation screen—no account creation. Include compliance footers for typical card marketing. Add an FAQ on credit pull timing, annual fee, and partner changes. Close with a compact risk disclosure framing availability as variable and not guaranteed, reducing later support friction.

Brand vibe: Premium and straightforward, prioritizing trust signals and clear disclosures over hype.

Constraints: Prominent legal disclosures; performance disclaimers; no stored calculator data.
title: AeroNest — Travel Card Pre-Launch

requirements:
Build a configurator that lets prospects model NimbusCRM’s impact and save a sharable quote without any login. Screen A: start in guest mode with a prominent “Save scenario” action that generates a shareable secret link. Screen B: inputs for team size, current close rate, deal volume, and average deal value with inline validation and helper text; show real‑time projected ROI and payback. Screen C: feature pack selection with price updates. Users can save multiple scenarios from the same device, rename them, and export a one‑page PDF with their assumptions. Include empty states (“No scenarios yet”), loading states for calculations, and error states for failed saves. Add a “Request demo” CTA that attaches the chosen scenario to the lead form. A lightweight internal page lists submitted scenarios for the sales team to prioritize outreach. Provide a simple audit note that records last edited time on the scenario card so conversations stay aligned.

Brand vibe: Analytical and crisp, with unobtrusive UI that highlights numbers and decisions.

Constraints: No login; scenarios persist via shareable links; include validation, empty/loading/error states; export to PDF.
title: ROI Configurator for NimbusCRM

requirements:
Create an application portal for a selective product leadership fellowship that avoids accounts. Screen 1: begin the application immediately; show an empty state if no draft exists and autosave locally, with an option to export/import a draft file to continue on another device. Screen 2: multi‑step application with validation (word counts, required links) and file uploads for resume and case sample; failed uploads show clear errors and retry options. Screen 3: recommender requests are captured as names and emails inside the form, then the system sends requests automatically once the applicant presses “Submit”; the portal displays pending/received status using the application ID. Applicants can revisit the draft locally until the deadline; final submissions generate a confirmation page with a receipt ID and a downloadable copy. A reviewer dashboard (separate internal role) lists submissions with filters by status and a two‑score rubric.

Brand vibe: Formal and organized, designed to reduce applicant friction while aiding fair review.

Constraints: No login; autosave drafts; validation and stateful reviewer workflow.
title: Fellowship Intake Portal

requirements:
Publish a thought‑leadership hub on reliability, incident response, and postmortems for CTOs and SRE leaders. The homepage features a concise positioning statement and top three pillar articles. Add topic filters (on‑page, no login), author bios, and a “How we write” style guide that explains blameless analysis and evidence standards. Include a newsletter sign‑up that routes to a mailing tool without storing data locally. Each article page must show estimated read time, structured headings, footnotes, and a lightweight glossary tool that reveals definitions inline on hover. Provide a resources page with downloadable runbook templates and an editorial policy page stating disclosure rules for client case studies. Add a “Pitch us” form with rate card request, but submissions only email the team. Close with a clear note describing how corrections are handled to reinforce trust.

Brand vibe: Rigorous and transparent, with sober design and careful sourcing as the default.

Constraints: Include editorial policy, glossary, and newsletter sign-up.
title: The Incident Ledger

requirements:
Hard Yields is a weekly macro and fixed‑income newsletter for operators and CFOs. Build a homepage that highlights the latest issue with charts as images and a concise thesis. Provide a back‑issues archive with filters by theme (liquidity, credit spreads, rate paths). Offer a “Primer” collection for new readers that links to five foundational posts. Add a subscribe module with double opt‑in and a brief data use note; no accounts or saved preferences. Integrate an editorial calendar block showing upcoming topics. Include a “What we got wrong” retrospective page reinforcing credibility. Article pages should support footnotes and linkable headings, ending with a short disclosures section covering conflicts and data sources so compliance review is simple.

Brand vibe: Sober and practical, aligning tone and visuals to institutional audiences.

Constraints: Double opt-in; back-issues archive; no persistent user data.
title: Hard Yields

requirements:
This is an essay hub on design leadership, hiring, and IC‑to‑manager transitions. Start with a manifesto header that defines the audience, then surface most‑shared essays, key frameworks, and a short reading list. Provide author profile and speaking topics with a simple inquiry form routed to email. Add a newsletter sign‑up and a “Start here” series for first‑time readers. Include a resources page with downloadable one‑pagers for portfolio reviews and critique rituals. Support a lightweight comments section via a third‑party widget that does not require site accounts. Add a short moderation policy and a clear approach to updates and errata to keep trust high.

Brand vibe: Candid and editorial, combining direct language with uncluttered presentation.

Constraints: No login; comments via external provider; include speaking inquiry form.
title: Work in Public

requirements:
Clinic Compass is a patient education hub for a multi‑clinic group covering preventive care, screenings, and common procedures. Build a topic index with age‑based and condition‑based navigation. Each article should include a plain‑language summary, preparation checklist, and “what to expect” timeline. Add printable PDF handouts and a glossary of terms. Provide language toggles for Spanish and English. Include a “Find a clinic” link that goes off‑site to the booking system but do not collect or store user data here. Add accessibility features and a content review date on each page. Finish with a brief editorial standards section that cites medical reviewers and revision history for accountability.

Brand vibe: Clear and reassuring, using plain language and inclusive design choices.

Constraints: Multilingual toggle; print-friendly handouts; accessibility statement.
title: Clinic Compass

requirements:
Create a reading app for educators and students to save, tag, and annotate articles without accounts. Screen 1: library list with search, filters, and an empty state prompting first import. Screen 2: article view with highlights, notes, and a “related readings” sidebar. Users can create collections, share read‑only links via generated URLs, and export notes to Markdown. Include validation for URL imports, loading indicators for fetch/parsing, and error states for blocked sources. Provide a preferences panel for font size, theme, and reading width. Enable export and import of the library and notes so progress can move across devices without accounts. A privacy summary explains what is stored locally and how to clear it to meet institutional policies.

Brand vibe: Studious and uncluttered, keeping attention on reading and reflection.

Constraints: No login; notes and highlights persist; empty/loading/error states.
title: Research Reader

requirements:
Build a submission portal for community op‑eds without requiring accounts. Screen A: author profile form with short bio, headshot upload, and validation for byline rules. Screen B: draft editor with autosave, word count, and a policy checklist before submit; drafts save locally and can be exported/imported as files. Screen C: submission status shows reviewer feedback, revision requests, and deadlines keyed to a submission ID displayed on confirmation. Editors have a moderation queue with filters and decision buttons. Include empty state messaging when no drafts exist, loading spinners when fetching, and clear error states for failed uploads. Authors can withdraw or resubmit before publication. Provide a “Publishing guidelines” page and email notifications on status changes. Add a transparency page describing selection criteria to reduce perceived bias and support community trust.

Brand vibe: Civic and fair, communicating openness while enforcing clear standards.

Constraints: No login; autosave; role-based moderation; validation and state handling.
title: Op-Ed Commons

task_description: Forge Labs — Product Studio Cases. lead
requirements:
Forge Labs designs and ships MVPs for venture‑backed startups. Build a portfolio site that opens with a crisp positioning line and a grid of selected case studies. Each case has a one‑minute read: problem, approach, outcome, and a single metric. Include a services summary, an engagement model section, and a transparent “How we scope in 2 weeks.” Add a short contact form that routes to email, no login or stored profiles. Provide testimonial quotes with client permission and a shortlist of logos. Add a methodology page describing discovery, design sprints, and delivery, plus a short procurement FAQ covering security reviews and MSAs to preempt buyer friction.

Brand vibe: Pragmatic and credible, signaling senior execution without theatrics.

Constraints: Case grid, services overview, and short contact form.
title: Forge Labs — Product Studio Cases

requirements:
PeakFrame specializes in brand and editorial photography. Create a portfolio with curated galleries, a short bio, and location availability. Include package outlines with day rates and an inquiry form for date and shot list—submit to email only. Add a client list, press mentions, and a simple “how a shoot works” timeline. Provide a delivery FAQ covering rights, turnaround, and revisions. No accounts, no client data storage. Add a “prep guide” PDF to reduce back‑and‑forth before shoots and clarify expectations.

Brand vibe: Elegant and restrained, letting images lead while copy stays precise.

Constraints: Price ranges visible; inquiry form; rights FAQ.
title: PeakFrame — Photography Portfolio

requirements:
CivicWorks publishes outcomes from neighborhood education programs. Build an impact site with a clear mission statement, annual highlights, and project pages detailing goals, partners, and measured results. Include donation links that go to a third‑party payment page. Feature a lightweight newsroom and a board/staff page. Add downloadable annual reports and a “How funds are used” pie chart as an image. Provide a volunteer interest form that emails the team. Add a transparency section with Form 990 links and program‑to‑overhead ratios to strengthen trust.

Brand vibe: Transparent and community-oriented, elevating outcomes over slogans.

Constraints: External donation processing; downloadable reports.
title: CivicWorks Impact

requirements:
A boutique litigation firm needs a results‑forward portfolio. Build a site that features categorized outcomes, representative matters, and attorney bios with admissions and practice areas. Include a concise “Why us” with differentiators and a compliance‑safe disclaimer. Add a contact form that sends via email only and a newsroom section for articles and press. Provide a clear conflicts policy link and accessibility statement. Include a jurisdiction map and a short FAQ on how to engage, retainer expectations, and timelines to reduce intake friction.

Brand vibe: Precise and formal, conveying competence and care without puffery.

Constraints: Prominent disclaimer; filterable matters; no client accounts.
title: Stature Legal — Results Library

requirements:
Create a secure client portal for an agency to share briefs, deliverables, and invoices without a login wall. Screen 1: organization selection and workspace introduction; new clients request a workspace with a short form. Screen 2: project list with statuses and an empty state if none. Screen 3: a project view with tabs for scope, files, feedback threads, and billing. Clients can approve milestones and upload assets. Include validation on required fields, loading states while fetching project data, and clear errors for failed uploads. Provide role‑based permissions that are encoded into each workspace URL. Add a notifications center and downloadable invoice PDFs. Include a simple SLA acknowledgment checkbox on approvals so expectations are explicit.

Brand vibe: Orderly and professional, making collaboration predictable and auditable.

Constraints: No login; stateful projects; approvals; empty/loading/error states.
title: Client Desk — Agency Portal

requirements:
Build a review app for video and motion projects that opens from per‑project links. Screen A: project dashboard opened from a unique project link. Screen B: a player with frame‑accurate comments, tasks, and version comparison. Clients can mark feedback as resolved. Include validation on comment length, drag‑and‑drop uploads with progress bars, and error handling on failed encodes. Provide an empty state for new projects and loading indicators while fetching versions. Exports compile comment timelines to PDF. Add a basic role system so producers can lock versions before delivery and prevent edits. Include a usage meter so buyers can understand plan limits before upsell conversations.

Brand vibe: Focused and modern, prioritizing clarity in review over ornamental UI.

Constraints: No login; persistent projects; robust upload states; exports.
title: FrameNotes — Video Review Room

requirements:
Sell digital synth preset packs for producers. Build a product grid with audio demos, pack details, and licensing notes. Clicking “Buy” opens a Stripe‑hosted payment link in a new tab; no site accounts or stored user data. Include a simple bundle promo and a FAQ on DAW compatibility. Add a support contact form that emails the team. Provide clear refund and download policies and a short creator bio. Include a “Try 5 free” sampler that captures email via an external mailing tool, setting expectations for future releases and updates.

Brand vibe: Crisp and audio-centric, with fast previews and minimal friction to purchase.

Constraints: External checkout only; audio demo players; license FAQ.
title: Arcade Keys — Synth Presets

requirements:
Offer a small catalog of trail tools and apparel. Create a lightweight store with 12 SKUs, size/fit guides as static pages, and a shipping/returns policy. “Add to cart” routes to a third‑party checkout; do not store user profiles. Include product spec sheets as PDFs, care instructions, and a sustainability note. Add a size‑finder chart image and an email capture for product drops. Provide a warranty blurb, a certified materials badge, and a simple fit‑question form that sends to support. Keep copy plain and practical to match an outdoor audience.

Brand vibe: Rugged and clear, emphasizing durability and straightforward information.

Constraints: External checkout; size guide; returns policy.
title: TrailSmith — Field Gear Mini-Shop

requirements:
BeanCraft ships rotating single‑origin coffee. Build a landing that explains roast profiles, sourcing, and delivery cadence. Include three plan cards with price per bag, but route “Subscribe” to a Stripe‑hosted checkout. Provide a roaster profile section, a brew guide PDF, and a shipping schedule. Add a “Pause anytime” explainer and an FAQ on freshness and grinding. No accounts or stored preferences on‑site. Add a short sustainability statement covering farms, certifications, and packaging to strengthen perceived quality.

Brand vibe: Warm and informative, pairing sensory cues with operational clarity.

Constraints: External subscription checkout; brew guide download.
title: BeanCraft Subscription

requirements:
GlowLab sells dermatologist‑designed kits. Build a focused landing with a diagnosis‑free quiz that runs entirely client‑side and resets on refresh. Present three curated kits with ingredient callouts and routine instructions. “Buy now” links to an external checkout; no account or storage. Include a dermatologist advisory board section, safety notices, and before/after images with consent. Add a shipping/returns policy and a contact form. Provide a short ingredient glossary for common actives to reduce support questions.

Brand vibe: Clean and clinical, using evidence-forward copy and restrained visuals.

Constraints: Client-side quiz only; external checkout; safety notes.
title: GlowLab — Skincare Kits

requirements:
Create a B2B portal for teams ordering branded merchandise without a login requirement. Screen 1: submit a wholesale application with tax ID validation; admins approve and provision ordering access via unique links. Screen 2: catalog with tiered pricing and inventory badges. Screen 3: order builder with saved carts, PO uploads, and address book. Include loading skeletons while fetching SKUs, validation on quantities and ship dates, and error states on payment failures. Provide order history, invoice downloads, and status tracking keyed to the unique link. Include a quote generator that saves drafts and a reorder shortcut for frequent items. Add an approvals flow for enterprise buyers so procurement can gate large PO submissions.

Brand vibe: Utilitarian and efficient, maximizing clarity at scale purchasing volumes.

Constraints: No login; persistent carts; role-based pricing; robust states.
title: ProMerch Wholesale

requirements:
Launch a small marketplace for paid video courses that works without user accounts. Screen A: catalog with search, tags, and an empty state for new visitors. Screen B: course detail with curriculum outline and preview videos. Screen C: checkout with card payment, then purchasers land on a progress dashboard that saves completion state and notes on the device; a receipt email carries a unique course access link for continuity. Include validation on purchaser details, loading indicators while fetching lessons, and error handling for failed video loads. Provide receipts and downloadable certificates. Add instructor tools for uploading lessons and setting prices, with draft/publish states. Include a refunds explainer and content quality guidelines to support learner trust.

Brand vibe: Straightforward and academic, designed for momentum from browse to learn.

Constraints: No login; saved progress; empty/loading/error states.
title: CourseMarket Learn

requirements:
A single‑location dental clinic needs a clear site. Provide services with transparent pricing ranges, insurance info, and clinician bios. Add a photo tour and accessibility details. The “Book now” button links to an external scheduling system; no accounts here. Include a new‑patient intake PDF and a post‑visit care library. Add a reviews strip and a contact form that emails the front desk. Provide a short emergency protocol note with after‑hours instructions and disclaimers. Keep all copy friendly and free of jargon to reduce anxiety.

Brand vibe: Calm and trustworthy, pairing warm imagery with straightforward information.

Constraints: External scheduling; downloadable forms; accessibility info.
title: Marin Dental Studio

requirements:
Neighborhood bistro site with seasonal menu, chef story, and gallery. Show hours, location map, and a special events note. Reservations link to a third‑party system; do not store user data. Include a private dining inquiry form and a press kit download. Add dietary tags on menu items and a newsletter sign‑up. Provide a short sourcing note on farms and seafood to strengthen brand values. Include a simple parking and transit guide to reduce booking friction for first‑timers.

Brand vibe: Cozy and modern, balancing warmth with clear details for easy dining decisions.

Constraints: External reservations; press kit; dietary tags.
title: CopperPan Bistro

requirements:
Create a service site for residential HVAC. List services, emergency response window, service area map, and financing partners. Add a “Get a quote” form with required fields and photo upload that emails the dispatcher only. Provide maintenance plan summaries and a short FAQ on warranties. Include badges for licensing and insurance. No accounts or stored quotes. Add seasonal tips and a “before your tech arrives” checklist to cut repeat visits. Keep copy practical and avoid jargon so homeowners can act quickly.

Brand vibe: Practical and reliable, focused on readiness and clear next steps.

Constraints: Service area map; license badges; email-only quotes.
title: FixRight HVAC

requirements:
Build a grooming salon site with service menu, breed‑specific notes, and a gallery. “Book appointment” routes to an external scheduler. Include a first‑visit checklist PDF, vaccination requirements, and a policies page. Add a loyalty punch‑card explanation and an email capture for reminders. No user accounts here. Provide a pricing clarity section by breed/coat to set expectations and avoid surprise charges. Include a short safety note about senior or anxious pets and recommended accommodations.

Brand vibe: Friendly and tidy, keeping information simple for busy pet owners.

Constraints: External scheduling; policy page; downloadable checklist.
title: Paws & Co Grooming

requirements:
Create a scheduling app for a salon collective that operates without logins. Screen 1: client details form capturing email and phone plus optional pet info; validation on phone and pet fields if the grooming variant is used. Screen 2: appointment calendar with stylist filters and availability. Screen 3: appointment detail with notes, reschedule, and cancellation. Clients see on‑device appointment history; stylists see daily load. Include empty states for new clients, loading skeletons for calendars, and error handling for failed bookings or payment holds. Send reminders and allow profile edits from the confirmation link. Add a stylist admin view to manage blackout dates, services, and pricing. Provide a simple reports screen so owners can track utilization and no‑show rates.

Brand vibe: Clean and efficient, optimizing for fast scheduling and fewer errors.

Constraints: No login; persistent profiles; full state handling; role views.
title: SalonFlow Scheduler

requirements:
Build a two‑sided portal for local tutoring that avoids traditional logins. Screen A: student/parent profile form with basics and subjects; validation on grade levels. Screen B: browse tutors with filters, availability, and an empty state when none match. Screen C: request session flow with confirmation and messages; confirmations include a unique request link for updates. Tutors manage bios, rates, and calendar; new tutor profiles go through an approval queue before appearing in search. Include loading indicators for search, error states for failed requests, and a simple session ledger with downloadable receipts. Store profiles, preferences, and history on device, with optional export/import for continuity. A safety page outlines background checks, messaging rules, and escalation channels for disputes.

Brand vibe: Community-minded and clear, supporting safe matches and steady progress.

Constraints: No login; tutor approval workflow; empty/loading/error states.
title: Neighborhood Tutor Hub
